name: How to Prepare Your Home for Bathroom Tile Installation

step.name: Step 1: Clear out all personal items, linens, and accessories
step.text: Empty every cabinet, medicine chest, shower niche, and vanity drawer. Pack everything into labeled plastic bins and store them in an adjacent room so the work zone remains completely clear of clutter.

step.name: Step 2: Establish a secondary bathroom routine for the household
step.text: Tiling involves demolition, substrate prep, setting, and curing time where the room is entirely off-limits. Plan shower and morning routines around another bathroom in the home or coordinate schedules ahead of time.

step.name: Step 3: Clear a wide pathway from the entryway to the bathroom
step.text: Remove rugs, decorative furniture, and wall hangings along hallways and stairwells leading to the bathroom. Installers need unobstructed space to carry heavy tile boxes, cement backer boards, and buckets of thinset.

step.name: Step 4: Confirm fixture choices and tile layout details in advance
step.text: Have your tile, grout color selections, and any new plumbing fixtures on-site or confirmed with your installer before work begins. Clarify pattern alignment, niche placement, and transition strips with your project manager.

step.name: Step 5: Provide access to water and electrical outlets
step.text: Ensure technicians have access to an outdoor hose bib or utility sink for mixing thinset and cleaning tools, along with grounded electrical outlets nearby. Discuss staging areas for wet saws in the garage or driveway.

step.name: Step 6: Plan for proper curing time after installation wraps up
step.text: Set expectations with your household to stay off fresh tile for at least 24 hours, and keep water away from new grout for roughly 48 to 72 hours based on manufacturer instructions.
